description: Inspect a 200A residential service entrance panel for code violations including workmanship, terminations, working space clearances, overcurrent protection, and panel configuration.
environmentDescription: A residential garage with a 200A service entrance panel, exposed conductors, breakers, main disconnect, and surrounding working space.

violations.description: Unsecured conductors in panel with poor workmanship

citations.text: Install electrical equipment tidily, with good workmanship.
Installation work is carried out by competent people with proper materials, and connections are secure and accessible for inspection.
citations.description: Unsecured conductors in the consumer unit with poor workmanship
citations.hintText: Look at how the conductors are arranged inside the consumer unit. Are they neat and properly secured?
citations.inspectionNote: Conductors inside the consumer unit are loose and crossing over each other. Good workmanship needs neat, secure connections.

violations.hintText: Look at how the wires are arranged inside the panel. Are they neat and properly secured?
violations.inspectionNote: Conductors inside the panel are loose and crossing over each other. The code requires neat and workmanlike installation.

violations.description: Aluminum service entrance conductor terminated on copper-only rated lug

citations.text: Terminations must make a solid connection without damaging the conductor, and connectors and terminals must be rated for the conductor's material.

violations.hintText: Check the main lugs. Is the conductor material compatible with the lug rating? Look for AL/CU markings.
violations.inspectionNote: Aluminum conductor is terminated on a lug rated for copper only. This can cause overheating due to dissimilar metal expansion rates.

violations.description: Working space in front of panel is less than 36 inches deep

citations.text: Working space in front of live parts must be at least as deep as Table 110.26(A)(1) requires; for 0 to 150 V nominal that is 3 feet.
Keep at least 1 m of clear working space about electrical equipment wherever it must be reached for operation or maintenance.
citations.description: Working space in front of panel is less than 1 m deep
citations.hintText: Measure the clear space in front of the panel. Is there at least 1 m of unobstructed working space?
citations.inspectionNote: Storage boxes are stacked within 24 inches (about 610 mm) of the panel face. The code calls for at least 1 m of working space.

violations.hintText: Measure the clear space in front of the panel. Is there at least 36 inches of unobstructed working space?
violations.inspectionNote: Storage boxes are stacked within 24 inches of the panel face. The code requires a minimum 36-inch clear working space.

sceneFact.note: Clear depth in front of the panel face

violations.description: Service disconnect located in an area not readily accessible

citations.text: Put the service disconnect where it is readily accessible, outside the building or inside near where the service conductors enter.
Put the consumer's service equipment where it is readily accessible and close to where the service conductors enter the building, and not in places such as clothes closets, bathrooms or stairways.
citations.inspectionNote: Service disconnect is located behind stored equipment and requires moving obstacles to access. It must be readily accessible under the code.

citations.text: Every installation can be isolated by a main switch at its origin, and the main switch must be accessible.
citations.description: Main switch located in an area not readily accessible
citations.hintText: The main switch must be accessible. Can you reach it without moving obstacles or using a ladder?
citations.inspectionNote: The main switch is behind stored equipment and needs obstacles moved to reach it. It must be accessible.

violations.hintText: The service disconnect must be readily accessible. Can you reach it without moving obstacles or using a ladder?
violations.inspectionNote: Service disconnect is located behind stored equipment and requires moving obstacles to access. Must be readily accessible under the code.

violations.description: 12 AWG conductor protected by a 30-ampere overcurrent device

citations.text: Protect conductors (except flexible cords) from overcurrent according to their ampacity.
A device protecting copper conductors from 14 AWG to 10 AWG is limited to 15 A for 14 AWG, 20 A for 12 AWG and 30 A for 10 AWG, and generally cannot be rated above the conductor's ampacity.

violations.hintText: Verify that each conductor's ampacity matches or exceeds its breaker rating. 12 AWG is rated for 20A max.
violations.inspectionNote: A 12 AWG conductor (rated 20A) is connected to a 30A breaker. The conductor could overheat before the breaker trips.

violations.description: Breaker operating handle center is mounted above 6 feet 7 inches

citations.text: Keep breakers and switches within easy reach: with the handle raised to its top position, the middle of its grip must be no higher than 6 ft 7 in. (2.0 m) off the floor or working platform.
In a dwelling unit, mount no branch-circuit breaker or switch with its handle more than 1.7 m above the finished floor. The main is excepted.
citations.description: Breaker operating handle is mounted above 1.7 m
citations.hintText: Check the height of the topmost branch-circuit breaker handle. In a dwelling it must not be above 1.7 m from the floor.
citations.inspectionNote: The top branch-circuit breaker's operating handle is at approximately 2.2 m (7 ft 4 in). This exceeds the 1.7 m maximum for a dwelling.

violations.hintText: Check the height of the topmost breaker handle. The center of the grip must not exceed 6 feet 7 inches.
violations.inspectionNote: The top breaker's operating handle center is at approximately 7 ft 4 in. This exceeds the code maximum of 6 ft 7 in.

sceneFact.note: Height of the center of the highest branch-circuit breaker handle above the finished floor

violations.description: Panel circuit directory is missing or has inaccurate circuit descriptions

citations.text: Label every circuit, and every change to a circuit, clearly with its specific purpose, in enough detail to tell it apart from all others.
A durable, legible chart, diagram or schedule at each consumer unit shows the type and make-up of every circuit.
citations.description: Consumer unit circuit chart is missing or inaccurate
citations.hintText: Look at the circuit chart at the consumer unit. Is every circuit clearly and accurately identified?
citations.inspectionNote: Several circuits are labelled generically as 'spare' or 'misc' while serving loads. A durable chart or schedule must identify each circuit.

violations.hintText: Examine the circuit directory inside the panel door. Is every circuit clearly and accurately labeled?
violations.inspectionNote: Several circuits are labeled generically as 'spare' or 'misc' while actively serving loads. The code requires specific, clear identification.

violations.description: More circuit breakers installed than the panel's rated number of spaces

citations.text: A panelboard must physically prevent installing more overcurrent devices than the number it was designed, rated and listed for.

violations.hintText: Count the breakers and compare with the panel's rated space count. Are tandem breakers used in non-approved locations?
violations.inspectionNote: Tandem breakers are installed in slots not designed for them, exceeding the panel's rated number of circuits. This overloads the bus bars.

violations.description: The {term:panel} is mounted inside a clothes closet, with coats hanging against it

citations.text: Overcurrent devices must not be placed where easily ignited material is nearby, such as inside a clothes closet.

violations.hintText: Look at what is stored right next to the {term:panel} enclosure.
violations.inspectionNote: The {term:panel} sits inside a closet with clothing and boxes hanging directly beside and in front of it. A fault or hot connection could ignite this material.

violations.description: The {term:panel} is installed inside a bathroom next to the garage wall

citations.text: In dwelling units (and hotel or motel guest rooms and suites), overcurrent devices other than supplementary overcurrent protection must not be located in bathrooms.

violations.hintText: Check which room the {term:panel} is actually standing in.
violations.inspectionNote: The {term:panel} is on a bathroom wall, a few feet from a shower and toilet. Moisture and the chance of a wet person touching it make this location unsuitable.

violations.description: A water supply pipe runs straight down past the top of the {term:panel}, through the space above it

citations.text: The space equal to the width and depth of the panel, from the floor up to 6 ft above the equipment or the structural ceiling (whichever is lower), is reserved for the electrical installation. Pipes, ducts, leak protection apparatus and other foreign equipment cannot be in it.

violations.hintText: Look at the space directly above the {term:panel}.
violations.inspectionNote: A copper water pipe and a drain run vertically in the area directly above the {term:panel}. A leak or condensation would fall straight onto live parts.

violations.description: The clear working space beside and in front of the {term:panel} is only about 20 inches wide because a water heater and a shelving unit crowd both sides

citations.text: The clear space in front of the equipment must be at least 30 in wide, or as wide as the equipment if that is greater, and may be centred or offset.

violations.hintText: Measure across the open floor in front of the {term:panel}, wall to wall.
violations.inspectionNote: A water heater and a steel shelf leave roughly 20 in of open width in front of the {term:panel}. The cover is about 15 in wide, so the standard 30 in minimum is what applies.

sceneFact.note: measured between the water heater and the shelf at the panel front

compliantFact.note: same measurement with items moved back

violations.description: A low soffit and duct run in front of the {term:panel}, over the standing spot, leave only about 5.5 feet of headroom in the working space of this new-construction house

citations.text: The working space must be clear from the floor to at least 6.5 ft, or the equipment height if taller. Exception: service equipment or panelboards of 200 A or less in an existing dwelling unit may have less headroom.

violations.hintText: Look up at what hangs above the standing spot in front of the {term:panel}.
violations.inspectionNote: A heating duct and soffit hang low in front of the {term:panel}, so a person must stoop to work there. Measure from the floor to the lowest object above the working space.

sceneFact.note: floor to underside of duct over the working space

violations.description: The {term:panel} door cannot swing open to a right angle because a bicycle rack and wall corner stop it partway

citations.text: The working space must allow equipment doors and hinged panels to open to at least 90 degrees.

violations.hintText: Try opening the {term:panel} door fully and see what stops it.
violations.inspectionNote: The hinged door of the {term:panel} stops at about 60 degrees against a rack mounted nearby. There is open floor in front, so the problem is only found by opening the door.

violations.description: A disconnect switch in the garage has no label saying what it controls

citations.text: Each service, feeder and branch-circuit disconnecting means is legibly marked to show what it is for, unless its location and arrangement already make the purpose obvious.

violations.hintText: Look at the disconnect boxes on the garage wall. Could someone tell what each one switches off?
violations.inspectionNote: A gray disconnect enclosure on the garage wall feeds equipment that is not beside it. The cover has no label or tag of any kind.

violations.description: A small branch-circuit neutral is red instead of white or gray

citations.text: An insulated grounded conductor of 6 AWG or smaller is identified by a continuous white or gray outer finish, or by three continuous white or gray stripes on other than green insulation.

violations.hintText: Follow the conductors that land on the neutral bar. Check the colour of each one.
violations.inspectionNote: A 12 AWG conductor with solid red insulation runs to the {term:panel} neutral bar from a 120 V circuit. Nothing about it is marked white or gray.

violations.description: A green conductor is connected to a breaker and used as a live wire

citations.text: Insulated equipment grounding conductors of the wire type have a continuous green or green-with-yellow-stripe finish, and conductors with that finish are not used as ungrounded or grounded circuit conductors.

violations.hintText: Look at which colours land on a {term:breaker} terminal. One of them should never be there.
violations.inspectionNote: A conductor with solid green insulation is clamped under a {term:breaker} terminal and carries load current. The ground bar next to it holds only bare and green wires from other circuits.

violations.description: A white conductor is used as an ungrounded (hot) conductor with no re-identification

citations.text: White, gray, or three-white-stripe insulation is for grounded conductors only. On circuits of 50 V or more it may serve as an ungrounded conductor only inside a cable assembly (for example a switch-loop supply) or a flexible cord, and in a cable it must be permanently re-marked a colour other than white, gray or green at its termination and wherever visible and accessible.

violations.hintText: Check the wire colours on the {term:breaker} terminals, not just the neutral bar.
violations.inspectionNote: A white 12 AWG conductor from NM cable (or a loose white THHN in conduit) is landed on a single-pole 20 A {term:breaker} in the garage {term:panel}. No tape or paint shows it was re-identified.

violations.description: The main disconnect at the service is not marked as the service disconnect

citations.text: Each service disconnect is permanently marked to show that it is a service disconnect, so people can tell the one device that cuts off the whole supply.

violations.hintText: Find the device that shuts off the entire house. Does anything on it say what it is?
violations.inspectionNote: A main {term:breaker} at the top of the garage {term:panel} is the only way to kill the whole supply, but it has no permanent marking calling it the {term:service-disconnect}. Only the individual circuit labels are present.

violations.description: A large black feeder neutral has no white marking at its ends

citations.text: A grounded conductor of 4 AWG or larger is identified by white or gray finish, three white stripes, or a distinctive white or gray marking put on at its terminations when installed.

violations.hintText: Look at the heavy feeder conductors. Which one is the neutral, and how can you tell?
violations.inspectionNote: A 2 AWG black conductor lands on the neutral bar of the garage {term:panel}. Its ends carry no white or gray tape, paint or sleeve.

violations.description: Rooftop solar feeds the {term:panel} but no multiple-sources plaque at the service shows where the solar disconnect is

citations.text: A permanent plaque, label or directory at each service equipment location (or an approved readily visible spot) shows where each power source disconnecting means is, lists emergency phone numbers of off-site entities servicing the sources, and carries the wording 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER'.

violations.hintText: The house makes some of its own power. Where would someone shutting down the building learn that?
violations.inspectionNote: A solar inverter on the garage wall is tied to the {term:panel} through a backfed {term:breaker}. The service equipment has no plaque or directory naming the solar source or where it is.

violations.description: A large black equipment grounding conductor has no green marking at its ends

citations.text: An insulated equipment grounding conductor of 4 AWG or larger that is not green must be permanently identified as an EGC at each end and at every accessible point, by stripping the insulation, coloring it green at the termination, or green tape or labels at the termination; conductor bodies with no splices or unused hubs are exempt.

violations.hintText: Check the heavy conductor that ends on the ground bar. How would the next person know its role?
violations.inspectionNote: A 4 AWG black insulated conductor runs from the main {term:panel} to the garage {term:panel} ground bar. Its ends have no green tape, paint or exposed bare section.

violations.description: A generator inlet beside the garage has no warning sign about the type of system it supplies

citations.text: Where a power inlet is used for a temporary connection to a portable generator, a warning sign near the inlet states the type of system the inlet is wired for, based on the transfer equipment: bonded-neutral (separately derived) only, or floating-neutral (non-separately derived) only.

violations.hintText: Find the plug-in point for a portable generator. Does anything tell the person plugging in which kind of generator it needs?
violations.inspectionNote: A generator inlet box is mounted on the exterior garage wall next to a transfer switch. There is no sign naming the neutral arrangement the generator must have.

violations.description: The outdoor air-conditioning condenser has no disconnect at the unit; the only way to cut power is a {term:breaker} inside the house, out of sight of the condenser

citations.text: A way to disconnect the air-conditioning unit must be placed where it can be seen from the unit and reached easily, and may be mounted on or inside the unit.

violations.hintText: Stand at the condenser and look around its walls and the nearby fence. Where would a technician switch it off before opening it?
violations.inspectionNote: The condenser sits on a pad on the far side of the house with the supply cable running straight into the unit and no switch box nearby. The only control is a {term:breaker} in the {term:panel}, which cannot be seen from the condenser.

violations.description: A vertical-handle disconnect on the outdoor air-conditioner is mounted upside down, so the handle's down position is ON and up is OFF

citations.text: General-use and motor-circuit switches and circuit breakers in enclosures must clearly show open (off) or closed (on). Where the handle moves vertically, the up position is the closed (on) position.

violations.hintText: Read the ON and OFF markings on the pump disconnect and compare them with where the handle sits.
violations.inspectionNote: The condenser disconnect enclosure is turned over so the ON marking sits at the bottom of the handle's travel. A person reaching for the handle would assume up means on.

violations.description: The detached shed is fed by a feeder from the house, but where the cable enters the shed there is no switch or breaker to disconnect the supply

citations.text: A building or structure supplied by a feeder or branch circuit needs a means to disconnect all ungrounded conductors that supply or pass through it. Under 225.36 a circuit breaker, molded case switch, general-use switch or snap switch all qualify.

violations.hintText: Follow the cable from the trench into the shed. What could you operate to turn the whole shed off from the inside doorway?
violations.inspectionNote: The underground feeder rises at the shed wall and runs straight to a junction box that feeds the lights and receptacles. There is no switch, breaker or panel at the entry point.

violations.description: The water heater is switched only by a {term:breaker} in the garage {term:panel}, which cannot be seen from the heater, and that {term:breaker} has no provision for a lock

citations.text: For a fixed appliance over 300 VA, the branch-circuit breaker can be its disconnect only if it is in sight of the appliance or can be locked open with the lock provision staying in place.

violations.hintText: Check how the water heater could be switched off safely while someone works on it. Is the control in view, or can it be locked off?
violations.inspectionNote: The water heater is in a closet on the opposite side of the house from the {term:panel}, and a wall blocks the view between them. The {term:breaker} handle has no lock-off clip or hasp fitted.

violations.description: The garage service equipment has seven separate {term:service-disconnect} {term:breaker}s instead of at most six

citations.text: A service normally has one disconnect; up to six service disconnecting means (switches or sets of breakers) are permitted for each service, and more than six is not. The limit is per service, not per building.

violations.hintText: Count the handles that cut off the whole house at the service equipment.
violations.inspectionNote: Seven separate main breakers sit side by side on the outdoor service equipment beside the meter, each serving a different load such as the house, the air conditioner and the water heater. All are fed from the same service.

violations.description: The one-family house's {term:service-disconnect} is rated 60 A, below the 100 A minimum

citations.text: For a one-family dwelling, the service disconnecting means must be rated at least 100 amperes, 3-wire, whatever the calculated load.

violations.hintText: Read the rating on the main device that switches off the whole house.
violations.inspectionNote: The enclosure of the {term:service-disconnect} is marked 60 A on its label and handle. The home is a single-family house with a normal 120/240 V supply.

violations.description: The condenser disconnect is screwed to the unit's removable service access panel and covers part of the equipment nameplate

citations.text: The disconnect must not sit on a panel designed to give access to the equipment, nor hide the equipment nameplate.

violations.hintText: Look at where the disconnect is fastened to the unit. Could a technician open the unit without removing it?
violations.inspectionNote: The disconnect enclosure is mounted over the compressor access cover and partly covers the nameplate. Removing the cover would mean removing the disconnect.

violations.description: A fence leaves only 20 in of clear depth in front of the condenser disconnect

citations.text: An air-conditioning disconnect must meet the working space rules of 110.26(A). At 120/240 V (0-150 V to ground) the clear depth in front is at least 36 in; the space is also at least 30 in wide and 6.5 ft high.

limit.quantity: clear working space depth in front of disconnect

violations.hintText: Measure the clear floor space in front of the disconnect, from its face to the nearest obstruction.
violations.inspectionNote: The disconnect on the condenser wall has a wooden fence 20 in in front of it. A person servicing it would be pinned between the fence and the equipment.

sceneFact.quantity: clear working space depth in front of disconnect
sceneFact.note: measured from the front of the disconnect to the fence

compliantFact.quantity: clear working space depth in front of disconnect
compliantFact.note: measured from the front of the disconnect to the nearest obstruction

violations.description: An unused knockout on the garage {term:panel} enclosure has been punched out and left open

citations.text: Unused cable or raceway openings in enclosures must be effectively closed so they protect about as well as the enclosure wall itself.

violations.hintText: Look closely at the metal sides and top of the enclosure for holes that nothing passes through.
violations.inspectionNote: A round opening in the enclosure wall has no cable, connector or plug in it, leaving a path to live parts. A listed knockout closure should be seated in it.

violations.description: An empty {term:breaker} space in the {term:panel} has no blank filler, leaving the opening exposed

citations.text: Unused openings meant for breakers or switches must be closed with identified closures or other approved means giving protection close to that of the enclosure wall.

violations.hintText: Check the front of the panel where no breaker is installed.
violations.inspectionNote: One {term:breaker} slot in the dead front is open with the bus stab area visible behind it. A filler plate should cover the space.

violations.description: A cable passes through the enclosure opening with no clamp or connector holding it to the enclosure

citations.text: Where cable is used, each cable entering a cabinet or panel enclosure must be secured to the enclosure. A narrow exception lets nonmetallic-sheathed cable enter the top of a surface-mounted enclosure through a long raceway.

violations.hintText: Follow each cable to the point where it enters the metal enclosure and see what holds it there.
violations.inspectionNote: A cable runs straight through a bare knockout with no connector or clamp, so it can be pulled or abraded on the edge. The cable should be held by a listed fitting at the opening.

violations.description: The flush-mounted {term:panel} cover has a wide gap between the enclosure edge and the broken drywall around it

citations.text: Where a flush-cover cabinet sits in a noncombustible wall surface, any broken or missing surface must be repaired so gaps at the cabinet edge are no more than 3 mm (1/8 in.).

limit.quantity: gap between enclosure edge and wall surface

violations.hintText: Check the wall finish right at the edges of the enclosure.
violations.inspectionNote: The drywall around the recessed enclosure is chipped back, leaving an open gap at the edge. Measure the gap against the 3 mm limit.

sceneFact.quantity: gap between enclosure edge and wall surface
sceneFact.note: measured at the widest point on the top edge

compliantFact.quantity: gap between enclosure edge and wall surface
compliantFact.note: measured at the widest point on the top edge

violations.description: Wall paint overspray has coated the bus stabs and terminals inside the {term:panel}

citations.text: Internal parts such as busbars, terminals and insulators must not be damaged or contaminated by foreign materials like paint, plaster, cleaners, abrasives or corrosive residue.

violations.hintText: Look at the metal parts behind the breakers, not only at the cover.
violations.inspectionNote: A thin layer of the same colour as the garage wall coats the bus and several terminal screws inside the enclosure. The paint can spoil breaker contact and hide heat damage.

violations.description: A conductor under a {term:breaker} lug has been nicked and some copper strands cut away where it was stripped

citations.text: Connections to terminals must be mechanically secure and made so the conductor is not damaged in the process.

violations.hintText: Study the bare copper where one conductor enters its terminal.
violations.inspectionNote: The stripped end shows a ring cut into the copper and a few strands missing. This reduces the conductor's cross-section at the terminal and weakens the joint.

violations.description: A {term:breaker} terminal screw is backed out and the conductor sits loose in the lug

citations.text: Connections to terminals must be a mechanically secure electrical connection, made without damaging the conductors.

violations.hintText: Read the small markings on the terminals, then check how the screws sit.
violations.inspectionNote: One terminal screw head stands proud of the lug and the conductor moves by hand. A loose joint heats up under load.

violations.description: The {term:panel} is mounted directly over the steps of the stairway leading from the garage into the house

citations.text: Overcurrent devices are not to be placed over the steps of a stairway, because someone servicing or resetting them would have to stand on uneven treads.

violations.hintText: Look at the floor in front of the {term:panel}. Is it level where a person would have to stand?
violations.inspectionNote: The {term:panel} is on the wall above the garage-to-house steps. A person resetting a {term:breaker} would have to stand on the stair treads.

violations.description: The main {term:breaker} is rated higher than the maximum ampere rating on the {term:panel}'s own label

citations.text: A panelboard must be protected by an overcurrent device rated no higher than the panelboard's own rating. The device can be a main breaker in the panelboard or one on the supply side of it.

violations.hintText: Compare the number on the main {term:breaker} with the rating printed on the {term:panel} label.
violations.inspectionNote: The main {term:breaker} handle reads 200 A. The {term:panel} nameplate inside the door shows a 125 A rating.

violations.description: The garage {term:panel} sits at vehicle bumper height beside the parking bay with no guard or protection

citations.text: Overcurrent devices go where they are not exposed to physical damage, so equipment where vehicles can strike it needs relocation or a guard.

violations.hintText: Think about what in a garage could hit the {term:panel}.
violations.inspectionNote: The {term:panel} is on the wall at the front of the car space. There is no bollard, guard or setback, and dents show on the cover.

violations.description: A fuse block in the panel has plain Edison-base fuse sockets with no Type S adapters, so any size plug fuse fits

citations.text: Edison-base fuseholders may be installed only where adapters make them accept Type S fuses, which resist swapping in a larger fuse. Once fitted, a Type S adapter is designed not to be removed (240.54).

violations.hintText: Look closely at the screw-in sockets on the fuse block. Could a larger fuse be threaded into any of them?
violations.inspectionNote: The fuse sockets are bare Edison-base screw bases with no Type S adapter ring in any of them, so any plug fuse within the base's rating would thread in.
